thread:
Samir: Heads up — kv-pool-2 triggered OOMs under low synthetic load at ~02:14 UTC. Memory climbed steadily after prefetch ramp; look like slab freelist churn + stuck reservations. Metrics: https://metrics.internal/redwood/allocs?pool=kv-pool-2 Heap dump: s3://redwood-infer/dev/dumps/3216549870-heap.tgz
Maya: Oncall. Pausing canary traffic and scaling down concurrent prefetchers now. Will mute alerting for this shard while we triage.
Priya: I can pick up triage on the freelist side. Noticed unusually high freelist fragmentation in last night's slab-scan. Will run an extended slab-scan + freelist histogram and post results. ETA: 24h.
Alex: I'll lead alloc tracing and repro. Plan: enable ms-resolution alloc samples, collect pprof heap+alloc_space, and run targeted fuzz that exercises prefetch cancellation paths. Hypothesis: race between reservation cancellation and freelist return makes refs sticky.
Jen: Ops will add a temporary runtime knob `--kv-freelist-coalesce=false` toggled to true only if needed, and set `--kv-max-residency=90MB` on canaries. We'll schedule a rolling restart for tonight to apply the guard. Creating ticket now.
Ops-Bot: Ticket INF-1190 created: "kv-pool-2 temporary residency guard + slab-scan" https://jira.internal/INF-1190 Assigned to Jen, target: 2026-03-28.
deploy-bot: Canary reverted to stable rev 781. Health checks passing. Monitoring window 45m. :white_check_mark:
Samir: Please also capture process-level vmstats and slab freelist snapshots at 30s intervals while repro runs. Priya, Alex: coordinate sample times so we have correlated traces.
Priya: Will run nightly slab-scan for 3 nights and post summarized histograms here. Also adding a small tool to map freelist spans to allocation stacks. Pushing prototype to https://git.internal/redwood/tools/slab-scan PR#834.
Alex: Found a candidate stack: prefetch.workerReserve -> kv_reserve.go:96 -> alloc_map.go:142; cancellation path leaves a lingering ref in slab freelist due to missing decrement in the fast path. Will include minimal repro and stack dump in the report.
Maya: Monitoring rule updated: alert if pool residency > 80% of guard for 10m, and page on >95% for 5m. I'll hold immediate paging if Ops-Bot sets a guard.
Jen: Ops: add a runbook snippet for emergency knob flips and include exact commands. For example: `kubectl patch deployment kv-canary --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"kv","env":[{"name":"KV_MAX_RESIDENCY","value":"90MB"}]}}]}}}'`
Samir: Action list (concise): - Priya: slab-scan histograms + freelist->stack mapping (24h) - Alex: alloc sampling, repro, patch proposal for safe release (48h) - Jen/Ops: apply guard + nightly slab-scan (today + 2 nights) - Maya: alerts and interim ownership (ongoing) - Samir: correlate with previous incidents and draft follow-up postmortem note (72h).
Priya: Added INF-1190 to my board and linked PR#834. I will post the first histogram by EOD.
Alex: Will grep for recent changes around freelist handling; suspect regression introduced in PR#834 (recent freelist micro-optimizations). Will attach commit diff and tests to the profiling report.
Jen: Ops will also add a temporary canary-level policy to auto-fallback canary traffic to stable if residency rises > 85% within 5m. Implementing as a Circuit Breaker in the ingress.
Samir: Scheduling a 30m sync in 48h at 09:30 to review Priya/Alex findings and decide whether to merge fixes or roll out mitigations. If regressions happen earlier, reopen this thread and alert. :eyes:
Maya: Noted. I'll keep paging rules as discussed and update the incident stub in the postmortem board.
Priya: First slab-scan uploaded: s3://redwood-infer/scans/3216550001-slab-histograms.gz — will summarize key buckets and freelist fragmentation in my next message.
Alex: Starting alloc-sample run now; will post profiler bundle to s3 and link here when done.
Jen: Nightly restart scheduled at 02:50 UTC. Ops-Bot will post rollout status in this thread.
Ops-Bot: Nightly restart kicked off for kv-canary nodes. Rolling restarts in progress.
Samir: Thanks team. Let's keep updates short in this thread; save detailed analysis for the postmortem doc.
